html:
The ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) is an agreement among the members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to cut tariffs on trade with each other. It was signed in Singapore in January 1992.

Twenty five years after ASEAN's founding, its members still traded more with Japan, the United States and Europe than with each other. China was opening up and pulling in foreign factories. AFTA aimed to make Southeast Asia one bigger market, so that investors would build there.

The main tool was a common scheme to bring most tariffs down to between zero and five percent. The six older members did this first; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia followed on a longer timetable.

AFTA grew into the wider ASEAN Economic Community in 2015. ASEAN also signed trade deals with China, Japan, Korea, India, Australia and New Zealand, and in 2020 led the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, one of the largest trade blocs in the world.
